subject: Cognitive Science
title: The Anchoring Effect
description: A fast breakdown of The Anchoring Effect for builders.

hook.text: Spin a wheel that lands on 65. Now guess what percent of UN countries are African. You'll guess high.

buildup.text: Anchoring means the first number you see pulls your estimate toward it—even if it's totally random.

discovery.text: Tversky and Kahneman showed anchors distort judgment even when people know the anchor is irrelevant.

twist.text: Retail pricing exploits this daily. A $500 jacket next to a $200 one makes the $200 one seem cheap.

climax.text: In salary talks, whoever names a number first sets the anchor. The whole negotiation orbits that point.

punchline.text: The first number wins. Choose it carefully.

quiz.question: What is the anchoring effect?
options: Initial numbers pull estimates toward them
People always choose the middle option
